L82: # Clinical Trial Service
L83: 
L84: Clinical trials are studies that explore whether a procedure, treatment, diagnostic test, or medical device is safe and effective. Trials help answer questions, and the answers can benefit both animal and human health because of the many diseases common to both. By participating in a clinical trial, you and your pet are helping us advance the future health and well-being of animals and humans.
L85: The Lloyd Veterinary Medical Center has outstanding veterinary expertise through its board-certified clinicians, faculty, and technical staff in a state-of-the-art facility. We have expertise and experience in conducting clinical trials and analyzing the data.

L89: # Clinical Trials
L90: 
L91: Submitted protocols are reviewed by both the Clinical Protocol Review Committee (LSU SVM Department of Veterinary Clinical Sciences) and LSU’s Institutional Animal and Care Use Committee (IACUC) with the intent to ensure that welfare and confidentiality matters are observed. These reviews are patterned on  “Good Clinical Practices” for conduct of clinical trials in human medicine.
L92: 
L93: 【27†FURTHER INFORMATION ON GOOD CLINICAL PRACTICES†www.fda.gov】
L94: ## Call for healthy dogs for atopic dermatitis study
L95: 
L96: Join the Journey: Help Advance Research for Healthier Dogs Worldwide!
L97: 
L98: The association between chronic passive lead and cadmium exposure and atopic dermatitis in dogs – a preliminary study.
L99: Heavy metals are present throughout the ecosystem. Heavy metal exposure is associated with a wide variety of health effects in humans and nowadays has become an important health concern. In humans, allergies have been associated with heavy metal exposure. Canine and human allergies share many similarities; therefore, the goal of our study is to see if there is an association between heavy metals exposure and skin allergies in dogs.
L100: We are seeking healthy (non-allergic) dog participants. Sampling is not painful and does not require sedation. At the visit, swab samples will be taken from various areas on the body. As well as 2 teaspoons of blood.
L101: Thank you for helping advance research that will improve the lives of dogs worldwide!
L102: 
L103:   * Healthy dogs with no signs of skin allergies or ear infection, or active/ malignant tumors
L104:   * One dog per household
L105: 
L106: If you are interested in participating, please contact Dr. McInnis and Dr. Apostolopoulos at navdlab@lsu.edu
L107: 
L108: 【7†LEARN MORE ABOUT DERMATOLOGY, EAR AND ALLERGY SERVICE】
L109: ## Call for puppies for osteopathy and vaccine trial
L110: 
L111: This trial consists of osteopathic treatments combined with DA2P (distemper, adenovirus type-2, and parvovirus) vaccine.
L112: 
L113: Osteopathy is a holistic and manual therapy that aims to rebalance all structures in the body, making it more efficient. It is a very popular preventive and palliative therapy for humans and animals in Europe.
L114: Our research aims to determine if osteopathic manipulation can boost the puppies’ specific defense when combined with classic administration of DA2P vaccine.
L115: 
L116:   * Unvaccinated puppies aged 8 weeks
L117:   * Not receiving other medical treatment
L118:   * Absence of metabolic disease (bloodwork will be run at the first visit)
L119: 
L120: Puppies will need to be brought in every 3 weeks for vaccine boosters and one last visit 4 weeks after the last vaccine for a total of 5 visits over 91 days.
L121:   * Free bloodwork
L122:   * Free vaccines
L123:   * Free osteopathic treatments

L47: Clinical trials often require patients to meet certain requirements in order for the trial to effectively pinpoint its research investigations. Some trials offer subsidies or funding for care, and each is carefully designed and reviewed for safety. Please ask your veterinarian to contact MSU for further information about any of the studies listed here.
